records.title: UWA Global Excellence Scholarship
records.deadline_display: A separate scholarship application is not required. Please submit an application to your chosen course. Our Admissions team will automatically assess your eligibility for a Global Excellence Scholarship once you provide your final transcripts.

source.as_of: 2027 intake (page states the scholarship is in place for 2027-2029 intakes)
source.raw_extract: How do I apply for the Global Excellence Scholarship? A separate scholarship application is not required. Please submit an application to your chosen course. Our Admissions team will automatically assess your eligibility for a Global Excellence Scholarship once you provide your final transcripts. | The scholarship is automatically awarded to those who are eligible based on ATAR/WAM requirements. | The Global Excellence Scholarship is an annual tuition fee discount for the normal full-time duration of the awardee’s course as specified in their letter of offer. | The Global Excellence Scholarship is in place for 2027 - 2029 intakes, so you can defer your commencement to 2028 with confidence that your scholarship and place at UWA is there for when you are ready to join us.
source.exact_deadline_wording: A separate scholarship application is not required. Please submit an application to your chosen course. Our Admissions team will automatically assess your eligibility for a Global Excellence Scholarship once you provide your final transcripts.
source.notes: Fetched the record's official_source_url directly; it is live. The page publishes NO scholarship deadline of any kind: a case-insensitive search of the fetched HTML for the string 'deadline' returns 0 occurrences. There is no scholarship application to apply for and no cut-off date; the award is made automatically on assessment of the applicant's final transcript. I deliberately did NOT use UWA's international course application deadlines, because a course-admission deadline for a different process is inadmissible evidence for a scholarship deadline. ROLLING was considered and rejected: the page never uses the word 'rolling' and never says 'no fixed deadline', and there is no application window to be open, so 'rolling' would wrongly suggest an applicant may apply at any time. UNKNOWN is the truthful classification, with the verbatim 'no separate application' wording preserved in deadline_display so the reason is visible to catalogue users.

source.notes: The record's official_source_url is live and I fetched it. It publishes four explicit regional final deadlines, all of which fell before today's retrieval date (2026-10-05): 1 April, 1 May, 15 June and 15 July 2026, i.e. between roughly three and six months ago. The page is still scoped to academic year 2026/2027 and no 2027/2028 dates are published anywhere on it, so this is an expired round on a record the catalogue still carries as open/active. Per the brief I therefore set outcome expired_mismatch, wrote NO date, and did not roll the dates forward to 2027. The only exact dates the page states are 1 April 2026, 1 May 2026, 15 June 2026 and 15 July 2026 (four different regional variants of the same final deadline - not a conflict); they are recorded here in notes only so that nothing is lost, and must not be copied into deadline_date. 'deadline_precision' at record level is 'exact' because that is the precision the source states; the field_mapping below deliberately proposes no write at all, because storing 'exact' with no date would imply a usable date exists. The page also says applications are 'assessed and awarded on a rolling basis', but that describes assessment order, not the closing dates, which the page gives explicitly.

source.notes: Fetched the record's official_source_url directly; it is live, and its in-page 'FAQ about Danish Government Scholarships' accordion is included in the quote above. source.notes: Read live in a real browser session on 2026-10-05 (the site is protected by a Radware Bot Manager that returns a CAPTCHA page to plain HTTP clients, so webfetch/Invoke-WebRequest could not read it; a headless-browser fetch of the record's own official_source_url did succeed). No closing date was taken from the 15 December 2025 news item: that page is behind the same WAF and returned a CAPTCHA on every attempt, so it is listed as examined-and-blocked. Nothing was inferred from the news headline or from any search snippet, and no secondary source was used.
